description.summary: sample image capture sources into a client surface

protocol.description:
This protocol enables clients to ask the compositor for a buffer that contains the contents of an image capture source. This buffer can then be attached to a surface that the client owns.
Instead of the client capturing and rendering the contents into its own buffer, this protocol moves the heavy work of rendering a captured image source to the compositor. The client requests a new sampler, gets the buffer for that sampler, and attaches that buffer to a surface that it owns. The compositor then fills in the contents of that buffer with the requested image. The compositor is responsible for keeping the content of that source up to date in the buffer as it changes.
The contents of the buffer are never sent to the host client. Only the compositor sees the image.
The protocol relies on ext_image_capture_source_v1.
The compositor may choose to restrict this protocol to a special client launched by the compositor itself or expose it to all clients, this is compositor policy.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: ext_image_sampler_manager_v1
interface.description:
A client uses the image sampler manager to request a new image sampler.
A sampler is created from an ext_image_capture_source_v1. This source can be backed by any source, including outputs, groups of surfaces, an individual surface, and more.

request.name: create_sampler

description.summary: create embedding for image capture source

request.description: Creates a sampler for the image capture source.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
This request should be called when the client will no longer use the ext_image_sampler_manager_v1.
Afterward, new samplers must not be created by this manager, but existing samplers must remain valid up until the point of their destruction.

interface.name: ext_image_sampler_v1
interface.description:
An ext_image_sampler_v1 object is used to retrieve a buffer that is backed by the contents of the image capture source that it was created with.
The image capture source is not mapped to a surface when the object is created. The client must call obtain the buffer via get_buffer, attach the buffer to a surface, and commit the surface for the mapping to occur. The surface of the client is subject to the wl_subsurface synchronization model.
The client itself never sees the contents of this buffer. Instead, the content is entirely rendered into the opaque wl_buffer object that is provided by the compositor.
The content of the buffer must automatically be updated by the compositor as the source image changes.

request.name: get_buffer

description.summary: retrieve buffer for image capture source

request.description:
Retrieve an opaque buffer backed by the image capture source that this sampler was created with.
This buffer must be attached to a surface and that surface must be committed for the mapping to be finalized.
The client must make this request following a size event in order to update the buffer to the new size.
Calling this while a buffer already exists for this embedding raises a buffer_active error.
If supported, the wp_viewporter and wp_alpha_modifier_v1 protocols should behave correctly on the surface to which this buffer has been attached.

event.name: size

description.summary: send when the size of the image capture source changes

event.description:
The size event must be sent by the compositor when the size of the backing image capture source changes.
The client should destroy any buffer that they are already holding and make the get_buffer request in response to this event. If the client does not request a new buffer, the compositor may no longer update the buffer that the client is holding.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Signals that the sampler should be destroyed.

entry.name: buffer_active
entry.summary: client already has an active buffer and cannot request a new one
